title: Prepositions
description: Learn prepositions for Grade 6: prepositions of place, time and direction, phrasal prepositions, and preposition vs adverb — with bilingual notes, examples, practice and tests.

topics.title: Prepositions of Place, Time & Direction
topics.concept:
Place tells where: in, on, at, under, over, above, below, behind, between, among, beside, near.

Time tells when: in, on, at, before, after, during, since, for, by, until.

Direction / movement tells which way: to, into, onto, towards, through, across, along, from, up, down.

The trickiest are in / on / at:

  • at — a point: at the bus stop, at 5 o'clock.
  • on — a surface or a day: on the table, on Sunday.
  • in — an enclosed space or longer period: in the box, in 2025.

examples.solution: on Monday, at 10 a.m. — 'on' for a day, 'at' for a clock time.

examples.problem: Direction word: The boat sailed ___ the river.
examples.solution: across (or 'along') — it shows the direction of movement.

recap: Place: in, on, at, under, between, near…
Time: in, on, at, before, after, since, for…
in = enclosed/long period, on = surface/day, at = point/time

topics.title: Phrasal Prepositions & Preposition vs Adverb
topics.concept:
Phrasal prepositions are groups of words acting as one preposition: in front of, because of, instead of, in spite of, according to, due to, by means of.

  • He was late because of the rain.
  • The car is parked in front of the gate.

Preposition vs adverb: the same word can be either. A preposition has a noun/pronoun after it (an object); an adverb stands alone.

  • He went in. → adverb (no object after it)
  • He went in the room. → preposition ('the room' is its object)

examples.solution: Adverb — 'in' has no noun after it, so it modifies the verb 'come'.

examples.problem: Complete with a phrasal preposition: The match was cancelled ___ the storm.
examples.solution: because of (or 'due to') — it shows the reason.

recap: Phrasal prepositions act as one unit (in front of, because of)
A preposition has an object (a noun/pronoun after it)
The same word is an adverb when it stands alone

questions.q: Which is a preposition of place?
Phrasal preposition meaning 'as a result of':
Preposition or adverb? 'The boy ran across.'
Spot the error: 'He has been waiting since two hours.'
Choose the correct option: 'The committee will look ___ the matter and report ___ Friday.'

options: She is married with a doctor.
She is married to a doctor.
She is married of a doctor.
She is married at a doctor.

questions.q: Identify the error: 'They were angry on the decision.'
questions.explanation: We are 'angry about' a thing (or 'angry with' a person), not 'angry on'.

questions.q: Choose: 'The thief jumped ___ the wall and ran ___ the field.'
questions.explanation: 'over the wall' (across the top) and 'across the field'.

questions.q: Rearrange: 'of / spite / in / rain / the / we / played'
options: We played in spite of the rain.
In spite we played of the rain.
We in spite played of the rain.
Of the rain in spite we played.
questions.explanation: 'We played in spite of the rain.' is correct.

questions.q: Choose the correct prepositions: 'She is senior ___ me but junior ___ the manager.'
questions.explanation: 'senior to' and 'junior to' — Latin comparatives take 'to'.

outcomes: Define a preposition and find it in a sentence
Use prepositions of place, time and direction correctly
Choose between in, on, at for place and time
Recognise phrasal prepositions (in front of, because of)
Tell a preposition apart from an adverb

intro.en: A preposition is a small word placed before a noun or pronoun to show its relationship with another word — usually where, when, or in what direction. In "the cat is under the table," under shows where the cat is.
intro.hi: संबंधसूचक अव्यय (Preposition) एक छोटा शब्द है जो किसी संज्ञा या सर्वनाम से पहले आकर उसका संबंध दूसरे शब्द से जोड़ता है — प्रायः कहाँ, कब या किस दिशा में। "the cat is under the table" में under बताता है कि बिल्ली कहाँ है।

real_life.situation:
You give directions to a friend:

You: Walk across the road, go past the bank, and my house is between the temple and the park.
real_life.why: Across, past, between are prepositions — each one fixes a position or direction. Without them the directions would be meaningless. That is exactly why prepositions matter.

error_detection.correct: He arrived at the station late.

sentence_correction.correct: The picture hangs on the wall.

rearrangement.answer: The cat is under the chair.

rearrangement.answer: We stayed home because of the rain.

rearrangement.jumbled: to / school / walks / he / every day
rearrangement.answer: He walks to school every day.

answers: on → a surface or a day
across → movement to the other side

reading.passage: On Sunday morning, Kabir cycled to the lake near his house. He left the bicycle in front of the gate and walked along the path. Because of the cool breeze, he sat under a tree and read until noon. At one o'clock he rode back home.

questions.q: Find a preposition of time in the passage.
Which phrasal preposition shows a reason?

questions.answer: to (the lake) — also 'along the path', 'back home'.

speaking: The keys are on the table.
We will meet at the station at noon.
He sat between his two friends.
We stayed indoors because of the rain.

writing.prompt: Describe your room in five sentences, using prepositions of place (on, under, beside, between, near).
writing.example: My bed is near the window. A lamp stands on the desk beside it. My books are under the shelf.

micro_quiz.explanation: 'above' shows position higher than the clouds.
'up' has no object after it — it is an adverb here.
'in spite of' is a group acting as one preposition.

challenge.q: Choose the correct prepositions: 'He has been ill ___ Monday, ___ three days now.'
Identify the error: 'She is superior than him in skill.'

options: Divide it between the three boys.
Divide it among the three boys.
challenge.explanation: Use 'between' for two, 'among' for more than two.
